_note: Visiting Waynesville (/visit/). Hand-kept. Facts only from official sources (village, township, county, ODNR, Chamber, Merchants, event organizers), each with a verified date. Organizations and businesses only; no private individuals. Checked monthly by scripts/check-resources.mjs.

items.name: Driving to downtown
items.what: Waynesville is tucked between I-71 and I-75, north of Cincinnati and south of Columbus, a short drive off the interstate at the Route 73 exit. Caesar Creek State Park is on State Route 73 east of the village (I-71 exit 45 or I-75 exit 38, per the county visitors bureau).

items.name: Parking downtown
items.what: Parallel parking along Main Street, angle parking on Miami and High streets, a public lot at North and Main, and shop lots open to the public. Please don't use the spaces in front of the post office on Miami Street or its side lot; they're for postal customers. Buses and RVs: park at the north or south end of Main Street.

items.name: Public restrooms downtown
items.what: In the center of downtown, between Lottie Mae's Cottage and Wendy's Treasures.

items.name: Bike racks
items.what: Next to LCNB Bank on North Main Street, at Veterans Park on South Main Street, and at McDonald's on South Main Street.

items.name: Sauerkraut Festival parking
items.what: During the festival, shuttle-bus parking is run by the Athletic Boosters at Wayne Local High School; follow the shuttle parking signs. The Chamber doesn't run or recommend the private lots around the festival.

items.name: Historic downtown shops
items.what: Known as the "Antiques Capital of the Midwest," with more than 60 independently owned shops and restaurants on Main, High and Miami streets and Scioto Square, and more along Route 73. Hours vary by shop, so check before you go.

items.name: DORA (outdoor refreshment area)
items.what: Inside the DORA, you can buy a drink from a participating bar or restaurant and carry it outside. Each shop decides whether drinks may come inside; look for a notice at the door.

items.name: Little Miami Scenic Trail
items.what: A paved rail-trail that runs through Corwin, next to Waynesville. Miami Valley Trails puts its length at 78 miles; ODNR runs about 50 paved miles of it, from Terrace Park to Hedges Road, as Little Miami State Park.

items.name: Corwin trailhead
items.what: The closest trailhead to Waynesville, in the Village of Corwin. The trail map shows parking, restrooms, picnic tables, wheelchair access and canoe access on the Little Miami River there. From Corwin it's 7 miles north to Spring Valley (and about 14 more to Xenia) or 14.2 miles south to Morrow. Caesar Creek State Canoe Access is just south of the village.

items.name: Caesar Creek State Park
items.what: A state park on State Route 73 east of the village, built around Caesar Creek Lake (about 2,800 acres), with boating, fishing, swimming, hiking and camping. Check the park's website for hours and beach details.

items.name: Caesar Creek Nature Center
items.what: The park's nature center, across the street from Pioneer Village (a separate building from the Visitor Center): ambassador animals, a bird-viewing area, a playscape, education exhibits and hiking trails. Free naturalist programs year-round, most Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays; see our calendar or call for hours.
items.sourceNote: Nature Center Association of Caesar Creek page (editor's link, 2026-11-07). It gives no opening hours.

items.name: Caesar Creek Visitor Center
items.what: The park's Visitor Center is a separate building from the Nature Center. Some events, like Owl Fest, meet here; check each event's listing for which location to go to.
items.sourceNote: Phone from the Nature Center Association's contacts list; the editor confirmed the two are separate locations (2026-11-07). Address and hours not listed there.

items.name: Caesar's Creek Pioneer Village
items.what: Volunteer-run living-history village of historic buildings, on land leased in the state park. Grounds open dawn to dusk; the buildings open during events.

items.name: Fox Hollow Rodeo
items.what: A rodeo every Saturday night, year round, rain or shine: semi-pro and amateur bull riding, barrel racing (summer only), and calf and sheep riding ("mutton bustin'") for young riders. No alcohol, coolers or outside food and drinks; tickets are non-refundable.

sections.title: Festivals worth planning around
sections.intro: Dates change each year; each festival's own site has the current schedule. Our events calendar lists them as dates are announced.

items.name: Christmas in the Village
items.what: The Chamber's holiday weekend downtown: 40-plus shops, about 1,000 luminaries on Main Street, a heated entertainment tent, Santa at the gazebo and a Parade of Santas. 2026: Fri, Dec. 4, 1–9 p.m. (shopping from 11 a.m.); Sat, Dec. 5, noon–8 p.m.; Sun, Dec. 6, 11 a.m.–4 p.m., with the Parade of Santas at 1 p.m.

items.name: Ohio Sauerkraut Festival
items.what: Waynesville's signature festival, on Historic Main Street the second full weekend of October. The 56th was held Oct. 10–11, 2026. No pets except service animals.

items.name: Ohio Renaissance Festival
items.what: A Renaissance village on State Route 73, open weekends plus Labor Day in late summer and fall, rain or shine. Parking is free; no pets (service animals welcome) and no outside food or drink. The 2026 season ran Sept. 5–Nov. 1.

items.name: Waynesville Street Faire
items.what: Saturday street faires on Main Street, run by the Waynesville Merchants Association, plus a Christmas Market edition on Dec. 6, 2026. See the merchants' calendar for dates.

items.name: Museum at the Friends Home
items.what: Local history museum in a 1905 Quaker boarding house, preserving the history of Waynesville and the surrounding villages.
items.hours: Wednesdays and Saturdays, 1–5 p.m., and by appointment

items.name: Underground Railroad walking tour
items.what: A guided walk of about a mile (roughly 90 minutes) through Waynesville's pre-Civil War Underground Railroad history, meeting at the gazebo in Waynesville Memorial Park. Booked online through the museum ($20 listed; non-refundable).

items.name: Self-guided historic walking tour
items.what: A walking-tour brochure and map of historic Waynesville from the Museum at the Friends Home and the Chamber of Commerce. Open the PDF online, or pick up a printed copy at the Chamber office or the museum (115 S. Fourth St.).

links.label: Walking-tour brochure (PDF, on the museum's site)

items.name: Waynesville Area Chamber of Commerce
items.what: Answers visitor questions and has the walking-tour brochure; runs the Sauerkraut Festival and Christmas in the Village.

items.name: Waynesville Merchants Association
items.what: Shop directory, events calendar and visitor guide for downtown.

items.name: Warren County Convention & Visitors Bureau
items.what: The county tourism office ("Ohio's Largest Playground"), with countywide attractions, dining and lodging.
